name: Strip plot
reader_question: How are individual observations spread within each group, and where does each group's centre sit?
relationship: Distribution of every observation per group on one shared axis, with a group median for orientation.
use_when: Each group has a modest number of observations that can all be shown
Spread, clusters and outliers matter as much as the centre
avoid_when: Groups have hundreds of observations — use histogram or box-interval
Only a summary range is available — use box-interval or range-interval

data_contract.notes: Explicit shared axis containing every observation
Every observation; the median and n are computed from them

units: One unit and one shared axis across all rows.

editable: Dots, median ticks, gridlines and labels are native shapes and text
not_data_bound: Dot positions are computed from the fixture and are not data-bound; there is no embedded workbook, so editing a value means moving its dot and relabelling the median
Vertical jitter is a deterministic function of rank, not a data value

table_alternative: A table of group, n, median, minimum and maximum, with the raw observations in an appendix.
variations: Box-interval when only five-number summaries exist
Histogram for one group with many observations
limitations: Vertical jitter has no meaning; only horizontal position is data
Medians from very small n are unstable and n is therefore printed on every row
Sample composition is not shown; unequal groups need caution

excluded_alternatives.reason: Not reproducible between builds; jitter is a deterministic function of rank
A smoothed density implies observations between the points that are not in the data
